posts.author: ideduce
posts.body:
Just a journaling spot for myself to stay motivated and to maybe finish something. I'm going to be using the default assets. It's more of a story telling game I think. It's not going to be a HUGE thing. That way I don't stress myself just something I want to play with and learn. Thank you for reading though <3
Guildfire
I want to make a anime-style rpg in the vein of Campfire Cooking or Shield Hero.
It starts out with a parallax of the sky and our protagonist, Troy, explaining the wars between monsters and humans. Humans are currently in hiding. He in a repurposed fort in the woods.
I had made 4maps currently for the fort
Face portraits
Troy - protagonist has 7 faces for emotion <3
Nerili Nicknamed Neri (Near-ree)- Fairy Party member 7 faces for emotion <3
Completed Orial Fort Maps
Orial Fort/Town (Like TutORIAL yeah, I'm not creativ,e or I am, but not for this place but I also like the name of it sooooo whatever XD)
Orial Fort - has all the buildings inside the fort, to run into it's very small though
Orial Inn - Troy has a goal of fighting enough monsters to have enough gold to sleep in here instead of the barracks one day.
Guild Hall - No one is allowed to leave the fort and assigned work in the fort that benefits the town. After doing a few fetch quests in town for food Troy will plead to become a mercenary of sorts. Unlocking a test. The guild basement has fire rats ready to test would-be adventurers. This is meant to scare people out of leaving the town. However, Troy has dreams of a comfy bed and a full stomach. So what if rats the size of a small dog can breath fire at him. He wants that fluffy pillow, dang it!
Orial Barrecks - yup, just a pick tent housing many people at once. The snoring is real. The ground is lumpy. The fetch quests are real. All motivation to GTFO and become a mercenary!
Shops to create
Weapons/Armor  Shop
Alchemy Shop
Resturant
I'm hoping when I make the quests I learn how to create switches/variables/and key items with the guild point system that will only be used in this starting area as a means to control the play from leaving.
0 quests are completed at this time
quests in town
Stop and Smell the Flowers - collect 7 flowers around the Fort reward 1 potion and 1 guild point
It's okay to stew - get 3 carrots for a  stew at the hotel (unlocks weapons quest) 1 guild point
Cool Sword - Gather water for the blacksmith to cool his weapons he gives Troy a sword warning him about a water slime that has tarrorized the fort and to take care of the issue. Fight one Slime! Get 1 sword and 1 guild point
My Cabbage!  - Collect 1 cabbage, fight 2 bats, get 1 potio,n and 1 guild point
Rescue a fairy - Troy has morals. Instead of using his new gold to get that one night in a hotel, he opts to use all his gold to purchase a fairy lady. He returns her wings to her so that she can find her own freedom. Never seeing a human be kind to any type of monster before she joins him to see what he's about and even informs him the forest had a war. It's restless and dangerous now because the Orc king has taken over the Fairy Queen's domain.
Fire Rats - with enough guild points, he ops to ask to be allowed to leave the fort. So he is tested in the guild basement to fight 10 rats, which will spawn a rat king

posts.author: ZombieKidzRule
posts.body:
I'd actually suggest taking a step back and recreating a bunch of basic tutorials following YouTube videos. You don't indicate what version of RPG Maker you are using, but there are a LOT of tutorial series for each version that cover most of the basics.
I'd recommend some for MZ, but I'm not sure what you are using.
I struggled at first too because I wanted to just jump right in and do things without a good foundation.
Using switches and variables is a very basic skill that is extremely important so getting those and other basic concepts down will help a lot.
If you step back now and invest a week or so just focusing on recreating basic tutorials, I think it will help tremendously.
I don't necessarily recommend my tutorial videos because I don't have a comprehensive series and I assume that the people watching already have a basic understanding of the engine.
But if you are using MZ or MV, I do have a couple of tutorials that might be helpful:
Anyway, good luck on your project and remember to enjoy what you do!
